messages:
alex_robinson: Pushed a Terraform change to add an eu-west-1 GPU nodegroup (p4). plan looked clean but terraform apply failed with quota error.
maria-gomez: Link to the plan? which module did you change?
alex_robinson: modules/k8s/node_groups.tf -> added module 'gpu-eu'. I ran `terraform plan -out=plan.tf` then `terraform apply plan.tf`. Error snippet:
```
Error: Request would exceed quota 'GPUs' for service 'ec2' in region 'eu-west-1'\n\n  on node_groups.tf line 42, in resource "aws_instance":\n  42: resource "aws_instance" "gpu" { ... }\n```
jamal_patel: AWS soft quota for p4s is tiny in eu-west-1, we've hit it before. You need a quota increase from support or switch instance type for now.
maria-gomez: Also seeing ArgoCD is stuck syncing cluster-config after your TF change — it errors with name mismatch for nodegroup label.
devex: Quick check: run `terraform state list | grep nodegroup` and `kubectl get node -o wide` against the cluster to see the nodegroup names; looks like naming drift between TF and EKS.
alex_robinson: I did `terraform state list` — tf state has module.gpu-eu.aws_eks_node_group.this but the cluster has auto-created node group name `eks-gpu-eu-legacy`. ArgoCD fails because our GitOps manifests expect `gpu-eu` nodes.
jamal_patel: That mismatch can happen if we've used mixed IaC (eksctl/console) and TF. We should import the existing nodegroup into TF or rename the tf resource to match. But first we need quota uplift.
sre-oncall: Can we pause the ArgoCD sync to avoid cascading rollouts? `argocd app set cluster-config --sync-policy none` until we fix state.
deploy-bot: [pipeline] argo-sync: cluster-config -> 1/3 resources failed to sync (NodeGroup: name mismatch) :warning:
maria-gomez: Another problem — trying to reapply the k8s addon (aws-node CNI) failed earlier in a different deploy. The addon upgrade is blocked because some nodes run older kernel and the addon helm chart's webhook times out:
```
Error: timed out waiting for the condition\nfailed to apply patch: webhook "validate.cni.aws" denied the request\n```
jamal_patel: We have two nodegroups with mixed CNI versions. The eks-addon controller refuses to upgrade because the webhook call fails on older nodes. Plan: drain the oldest nodegroup, reprovision new nodes with the same CNI image, then re-run addon upgrade.
alex_robinson: I can refactor TF to manage the addon with `aws_eks_addon` instead of our previous helm wrapper. Will add `wait_for_no_resources = true` and explicit `addon_name = "vpc-cni"` so ArgoCD doesn't try to helm-upgrade it separately.
maria-gomez: Sounds good. @jamal_patel can you request quota uplift? we can't create the p4 nodegroup until that's approved. :pray:
jamal_patel: Submitted AWS support case #12345678 requesting GPU quota increase in eu-west-1. ETA from support usually 24-48h but I also added Business Priority.
devex: Also suggest we add a CI preflight: `make tf-check && argocd app diff cluster-config` in GitLab CI to catch drift before merging. I'll open an MR for that today.
alex_robinson: I'll hold the TF MR behind a feature flag and set the ArgoCD app annotation `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-10"` so addons get upgraded before nodegroups. After quota is confirmed we'll run a canary: create one gpu node, run smoke tests `./infra/k8s/smoke.sh` and then scale.
sre-oncall: If the webhook keeps blocking, we can temporarily set `spec.ignoreWebhookFailures: true` for the addon upgrade, but only as last resort. Make sure to document rollback steps: `kubectl rollout undo daemonset aws-node -n kube-system`.
maria-gomez: Ok — action items: 1) jamal - follow up on quota case. 2) alex - MR to manage addon via eks_addon + guarded apply. 3) devex - CI preflight MR. 4) me - pause ArgoCD sync for cluster-config until we confirm state. I'll annotate the app and monitor.
alex_robinson: I'll also add a quick tf-import script to reconcile existing nodegroups: `scripts/tf-import-nodegroup.sh <cluster> <aws-name> <tf-resource>` so we avoid future naming drift.
jamal_patel: Noted. I'll post updates in this thread when support replies. If super urgent we can provision in another region with capacity but that complicates latency for eu users.
maria-gomez: Thanks team. Keep the thread updated, and let's avoid manual console fixes unless absolutely necessary. :eyes:
